title: E2. String (Hard Version)
statement:
This is the hard version of the problem. The difference between the versions is that in this version, the constraints on k and q are larger. You can hack only if you solved all versions of this problem.

Define popcount_k(m) as the sum of all digits of m in base k.

Define a base-k integer s=overlines_1s_2⋯ of infinite length, where the i-th digit of s is s_i=(popcount_k(i) bmod k).

There are q queries. Each query consists of three integers l, r, and n (all of them are given in decimal form), as well as a base-k integer t with n digits. Note that t may have leading zeros. Consider t as a string, and your task is to find the number of occurrences of t in the string s_ls_{l+1}… s_r.

For digits greater than or equal to decimal mathtt10, uppercase and lowercase letters are used. Specifically, the uppercase letters {mathttA, B,…,Z} represent the decimal values {mathtt10, 11,…,35}, and the lowercase letters {mathtta, b,…,z} represent the decimal values {mathtt36, 37,…,61}.

The first line of the input contains two integers k and q (2≤ k≤ 62, 1≤ q≤ 10^4) — the base and the number of queries.

Each query contains two lines. The first line contains the three integers l, r, and n (1≤ l≤ r≤ 10^17, 1≤ n≤ 2·10^6).

The second line contains the base-k integer t with n digits (t_i∈{mathtt0,1,…,9,A,B,…,Z,a,b,…,z}).

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2·10^6.

For each query, output a single integer — the answer to the query.

Denote the substring s_ls_{l+1}… s_r as s[l;r].

In the first example, k = 3, s = mathtt12120201120201012201120012…, s[5;17] = mathtt0201120201012, and t = mathtt201 appears a total of 2 times in s[5; 17]. Their indices in the string s are s[6; 8] and s[12; 14]. And t = mathtt01 appears 3 times. Their indices in the string s are s[7;8], s[13;14], and s[15;16].

For the second example, k=10, s[1;20] = mathtt12345678912345678902, and t = mathtt123456789 appears a total of 2 times in s[1;20].

Input:
```
3 45 17 32015 17 2011239 1231231209 501201123002 231203 41202
```

Output:
```
2
3
21046666
8325
```

Input:
```
10 31 20 912345678915 20332 36781234 56789 201
```

Output:
```
2
1625
5000
```

Input:
```
62 11 100000 620123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz
```

Output:
```
25
```
